transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-14 16:00 UTC; Duration ~38m; Attendees: Maya, Carlos (Redwood); Olivia, Marcus, Priya (Verdant)

Summary: Discovery focused on embeddings/re-ranking architecture. Verdant currently uses a hybrid search stack; evaluating Redwood for hosted or dedicated inference to reduce latency and cost for rerank step. Security and VPC requirements discussed. Agreed next steps: send pricing, benchmark template, schedule POC.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. How're you all doing?
00:07 Olivia: Good thanks, excited to get into this.
00:10 Marcus: Hey, yeah, thanks for setting this up.
00:14 Priya: Hi, thank you.
00:16 Maya: Quick agenda — we want to understand your current pipeline (vector DB, rerank, traffic/QPS), any latency/cost constraints, and then walk through hosted vs dedicated vs private options for embeddings and reranking. Sound ok?
00:29 Olivia: Yep, that's perfect. I'll kick off with our stack. We currently use OpenSearch for initial retrieval with BM25, then a reranker that does cross-encoder scoring using a 1k token context. We store embeddings in Pinecone for some prototypes but it's not fully in prod.
00:46 Maya: Got it. When you say reranker, is that a bi-encoder followed by cross-encoder or a single-stage?
00:52 Marcus: It's a two stage: dot-product retrieval from OpenSearch/Pinecone to get top 200, then a cross-encoder model (we call it re-rank) that scores the 200 and we return top 5.
01:04 Carlos: And what's your current QPS and latency SLO for the rerank step?
01:08 Marcus: Peak QPS is around 12 qps, average 4 qps. We want 99th percentile latency for rerank under 250ms ideally, but we'll tolerate up to 500ms for heavy queries.
01:19 Maya: That's helpful. For cross-encoder rerank, that latency target at 12qps points toward dedicated GPU capacity or lower-precision quantized models on hosted with batching. Do you have an idea of model size — how many parameters or embedding dimensionality?
01:33 Marcus: We're using a medium cross-encoder; embeddings are 768 dims for the bi-encoder, cross-encoder is a 220M-ish model. We're also exploring 1024 and 1536 dims for better recall on long docs.
01:46 Priya: From a security perspective, we will need SOC2, SSO/SAML, and the option to run in our VPC. Ideally customer-managed KMS for any private deployment.
01:56 Maya: That's standard for our enterprise customers — Redwood Private supports VPC and BYOK/KMS, and we can provide SOC2 artifacts. We'll follow up with the security pack.
02:04 Olivia: Great. On the vector DB side, if we move to a hosted Redwood embedding service, do you recommend keeping Pinecone or migrating embeddings to your managed store?
02:15 Carlos: We usually recommend keeping vector DB separated. Many customers use Redwood for embedding generation and model inference but persist vectors in Pinecone, Weaviate, or OpenSearch, depending on their features. The key is we optimize the rerank runtime — we can accept top-K results from any DB via API.
02:30 Marcus: So integration is basically: we call Redis or Pinecone for nearest neighbors, then send the 200 candidates to Redwood rerank endpoint?
02:36 Carlos: Exactly. We support batching and streaming responses. For 200 candidates at 12 QPS, we typically recommend batching 8-16 queries and running concurrent workers.
02:45 Olivia: You mentioned dimensionality — what's the unit-cost impact between 768 and 1536 dims?
02:50 Maya: Embedding generation cost scales roughly linearly with input size and model size. Storage and nearest-neighbor retrieval cost in vector DB increases with dimensionality. For reranking, higher-dim bi-encoder may improve recall (so fewer candidates), which can reduce overall rerank compute. It's a tradeoff.
03:05 Marcus: Any guidance on hybrid search? We want BM25 + embeddings. How does Redwood fit in?
03:10 Carlos: Hybrid is common — use BM25 to retrieve lexical matches, combine with vector similarity, and then send top-N to cross-encoder. Redwood focuses on the rerank step; we don't force you to change your retrieval. We also have examples for rerank thresholds to minimize tokens processed — like early stopping if top scores exceed threshold.
03:26 Priya: On private deployments, how isolated is the control plane? We need to know what network flows out to Redwood.
03:34 Maya: For Redwood Private/VPC, control plane can be customer-managed or we offer a private control plane. Data plane (inference) can be fully in your VPC. The control plane telemetry can be configured to not send PII — we will share the network diagram.
03:46 Priya: Good. We'll need that before legal signs off.
03:49 Olivia: For benchmarking, what metrics should we collect? We have a sample dataset ~100k docs and 10k queries.
03:56 Carlos: Ideal benchmark artifacts: sample docs, expected top-K (gold labels), a list of queries, and expected QPS. We'll run both throughput (bulk rerank qps) and cold-latency tests. We'll provide a template.
04:08 Marcus: For the cross-encoder, do you run KV cache or anything to speed up repeated tokens?
04:13 Carlos: For generation tasks we do KV cache; for classification/rerank mostly compute-bound, so we rely on batching, kernel optimizations, and quantized models. Our runtime selects kernels and quant paths automatically based on model architecture.
04:26 Olivia: If we wanted to go hosted first and then Dedicated later, how seamless is it to migrate?
04:32 Maya: Very seamless — same API and model versions. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. Most customers prototype on hosted and then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost.
04:44 Marcus: Pricing — ballpark per-qps or per-token numbers would help.
04:48 Maya: I'll send a hosted pricing sheet and an example Dedicated commit with GPU type and expected QPS. For rerank, we often price per inference request or per compute-minute depending on configuration. I'll include example math for your 12 qps workload.
04:59 Priya: Any compliance gaps we should be aware of?
05:02 Maya: SOC2, SSO, SAML, RBAC are supported. For FedRAMP or special programs, we'd evaluate on a case-by-case basis. KMS and audit logs are available on Dedicated and Private.
05:12 Olivia: About latency again — you said batching helps but could increase latency. How do you tune for 99p latency?
05:18 Carlos: We tune batching policies by max latency target and sequence length distribution. For rerank short inputs, we can do aggressive batching without hurting p99 much. For long sequences (you mentioned 1k tokens), we may need dedicated instances sized for throughput. Also prefix/KV caching helps for chat-like stateful workloads but less so for one-off rerank.
05:37 Marcus: Do you support fp16 or int8 quantization for cross-encoder weights?
05:41 Carlos: Yes, quantization profiles exist. int8 with some calibration typically gives large cost savings with small accuracy hit; we'll recommend model/quant pairs for your eval set.
05:49 Olivia: What about streaming outputs — not relevant for rerank but good to know for other features.
05:53 Maya: We support streaming and tool/function calling in the API; not central to rerank but part of the product.
05:58 Marcus: Any examples of similar customers?
06:01 Maya: We have a couple search-heavy customers in SaaS and e-commerce that do BM25 + vector retrieval + Redwood rerank. Happy to share anonymized benchmarks.
06:10 Olivia: That would help.
06:12 Carlos: Also, on the vector DB integration, we support efficient top-K callers — you can send candidate IDs and embeddings or we can pull candidates via a small integration layer.
06:25 Marcus: For throughput testing, do you recommend synthetic or real traffic?
06:28 Carlos: Real traffic is best for tail latency. Synthetic can help scale tests. We usually run both. We'll share our benchmark harness.
06:35 Priya: Legal process — how long from POC to contract? Our procurement typically takes 8-12 weeks after successful POC.
06:44 Maya: That aligns with most customers. POC 2-4 weeks, then procurement + security review. We'll support with security docs and standard SLAs.
06:51 Olivia: Can we talk about expected unit economics? For example, if we reduce candidates from 200 to 100 with a better bi-encoder, does that cut cost roughly in half?
06:59 Carlos: Roughly yes — rerank cost is linear in number of candidates and model compute. If your recall allows reducing candidates, you'll see direct savings. Also caching and early-stopping heuristics reduce compute. We'll model that in the benchmark.
07:15 Marcus: What about index updates — we reindex daily with 50k doc changes, any implications?
07:20 Carlos: That's fine for most vector DBs; for ours we'd recommend incremental updates. Reindex frequency mainly affects freshness, not rerank runtime.
07:29 Olivia: Ok, let's get practical. We'll do a POC: 2-week benchmark, tests for 12 QPS peak, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, and quality (MRR, recall@5).
07:38 Maya: Sounds good. Proposed scope: Redwood will run hosted benchmark using your sample dataset first. If results look promising we can propose Dedicated sizing.
07:47 Marcus: For hosting, how much data do we need to share? We can't share PII in some docs.
07:52 Priya: Right, we'll scrub any PII; Marcus will produce a synthetic set if needed, otherwise masked real data.
07:58 Maya: Great. We'll send the benchmark template and a checklist on data sanitization.
08:04 Olivia: Anything else on integration? We use REST APIs and have a thin orchestration layer; latency between our app and Redwood endpoints might add 20-30ms.
08:13 Carlos: Network latency is considered — Dedicated in your region or VPC deployment reduces cross-region hops. We'll include region options in the proposal.
08:22 Marcus: Any hard limits on candidate list size? We sometimes pass 500 candidates for complex queries.
08:27 Carlos: We can handle 500 but cost scales; for practical latency targets we generally recommend keeping candidate lists smaller but we can test your 500-case in the POC.
08:36 Olivia: That helps.
08:38 Priya: I'll need the security pack by Friday to kick procurement.
08:41 Maya: We'll prioritize that.
08:43 Maya: Quick recap — action items: I send pricing + hosted vs dedicated comparison; Carlos shares benchmark template and suggested config; Marcus provides sample dataset and expected QPS; Priya confirms compliance doc list. POC kickoff target week of 1/25.
08:57 Olivia: Sounds good. Thanks all.
09:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (Redwood Dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated, Pinecone mis-transcribed as "pine cone" in some places), speaker overlaps, filler words.

References shared: "benchmark_template.xlsx" (Carlos), "security_pack_SOC2.pdf" (Maya), pricing_sheet_hosted_vs_dedicated.xlsx (Maya).
